title: Edmund Hall and Bob Watts
summary: Brief talk on Edmund Hall's New Orleans days and trumpeter Bob Watts, who left for Texas around 1926.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: I didn't listen to Edmund Hall when he was down here. Edmund? Yeah. I knew Edmund. Who was he with?
I don't know who Edmund played with. I don't know. I just remember now who Edmund played with. Did you hear anybody say?
No. I don't know too much except he was with Buddy. That's the one.
That wasn't with me. I wasn't with him.
And what about Bob Watts? You tell me about him coming out from Texas.
Oh, a little Bob. A little trumpet player? Yeah. Bob's a nice little trumpet player.
He's from the street back in the battlefield. The woman in Bedita. He's out in the U.S.

I don't know who Bob played with around here. He left early, you know. He left while I was playing on the roof guard around twenty-seven, twenty-six to twenty-seven. I was surprised when I went out from Texas and seen him out there. Because I didn't get out there until thirty-six. He said he left New Orleans around twenty-six. Used to work at Morris' Music Shop, you know.
